Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-region ask and replication model

Hi Avery / Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. To summarize CloudTailor's ask: we need guaranteed steady-state throughput for our inference pipelines in US-EAST and US-WEST (low- to mid-µs P50 token latencies for short calls) with a DR plan that is either warm-standby or active-active. We are evaluating 2 sizing options:

- Option A (active-active): independent reserved pools in each region sized to handle 60% of peak traffic locally, with cross-region routing for spikes.
- Option B (primary + failover): primary pool sized for full traffic in US-EAST, with a smaller passive (standby) pool in US-WEST plus fast cross-region failover.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) How do you price active-active replication (synchronous KV replication vs async cache warm-up) and what are the per-region commit discounts?
2) Minimum committed GPUs / pool sizing granularity (can we commit fractional throughput units or must we buy whole GPU-equivalents?).
3) SLAs and throughput guarantees per region and behavior during cross-region failover (how do you bill tokens served during failover?).

Attached is our internal traffic profile and a rough expected 90th percentile token/sec per region. Can you propose a clean cost/benefit comparison for A vs B?

Thanks,
Ana
Ana Gomez
Head of Infra & ML Platform
CloudTailor

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-region ask and replication model

Ana — great summary and thanks for sharing the profile. High-level answers below; I'll follow with a short worksheet.

1) Pricing for active-active: we price per-region reserved capacity (committed GPU-equivalents) plus an optional replication surcharge for active-active that covers continuous KV/replication bandwidth and cross-region redundancy orchestration. In practice the surcharge is a percent of the sum of region commits. For synchronous replication (rare) we'd add a higher networking/replication fee; for async cache-warmup we charge a smaller ongoing replication monitoring fee + occasional cross-region egress for refreshes.

2) Commit granularity: we offer two commit units — GPU-equivalents (whole units) and throughput units (TUs). TUs map to sustained token/sec at a standard sequence length and let you commit fractional capacity. Customers can mix: e.g., commit 10 GPUs + 1200 TUs. Committed pricing gives meaningful discounts vs on-demand.

3) Failover billing: during a failover event we bill actual usage in the region that serves traffic at the on-demand rate unless you have pre-allocated standby reserves. If you run active-active with balanced commits, normal serving is billed against the committed pools. We also provide configurable automatic fallback to compatible lower-cost model variants if you want cost-aware failovers.

I'll attach a worksheet with a side-by-side for your two options (approx numbers). Action items: Avery and I will model the traffic you sent and return a v3 pricing workbook by EOD Fri. Marissa, can you make sure we include a line item for cross-region egress and an optional DR test run fee?

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-region ask and replication model

Ana — throwing some structure around Ben's note. Attached is a proposed packaging approach. Key tradeoffs:

- Active-active (Option A): higher committed cost (you pay for meaningful commits in both regions) but lowest latency and no cold-warm warm-up risk. Recommended if both regions regularly serve significant, independent traffic. Replication surcharge (we propose 12% of committed spend across regions in the quote) for continuous KV sync and cross-region orchestration.

- Primary + standby (Option B): lower committed spend overall; you only pay full commits where primary is sized. Standby pool can be billed as a reduced-commit (30–40% of primary) or as a paid-on-failover on-demand pool. DR test runs (we recommend quarterly) are a billable professional-service to rehearse failover.

Sizing notes: we can represent pool sizing as either GPUs (N x A100-equivalents) or TUs. For your profile a hybrid commit (4 GPUs east + 900 TUs west) looks cost-effective. We also recommend a small burst buffer in the opposite region for absorbing short spikes (billed as metered bursts).

Next steps:
1) Ben to share line-by-line cost with the 12% replication surcharge and a variant with 6% (async warm-up) for comparison.
2) Marissa to assemble SOW draft and include test-run cadence.
3) Ana to confirm which DR model CloudTailor prefers and whether procurement wants a single consolidated invoice or per-region bills.

Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — reviewed with procurement. A few clarifying points:

- CloudTailor leans to Option B (primary + failover) to reduce committed spend; we're open to a greenfield hybrid later.
- Procurement requests the following concessions for a 12‑month commit: 10% off list committed pricing, waived first DR rehearsal fee, and a 60‑day SLA rebate window for major incidents during the first 6 months.
- Can you confirm that standby pool commit can be a TU-only commit (no GPUs) and that billing will treat standby as a lower-tier commit with pro-rated charge during failover?

Please confirm and we'll get legal in parallel.

Ana

Ana — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and our position:

- Standby as TU-only: yes, standby can be TU-only. We will reflect that in the workbook. During failover, standby TU usage will apply against committed TUs; any excess is billed at the on-demand TU rate.
- 12-month concessions: we can agree to a 10% committed discount (applies to committed GPU and TU list prices) and waive the first DR rehearsal fee. The 60-day SLA rebate window is reasonable — we'll include a limited first-6-month rebate clause in the SOW (subject to legal review).
- We'll provide a variant line in the pricing workbook for a 6% replication surcharge (async warm-up) vs the default 12% (active-active).

Action: Ben / Marissa will issue the updated workbook + SOW (final draft) by EOD tomorrow. If procurement confirms the single-invoice preference we'll lock that option into billing.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.
